title: What We Learned from Using LLMs in Pinterest — Mukuntha Narayanan, Han Wang, Pinterest
talk_summary: Pinterest engineers describe using a large LLM cross-encoder as a relevance teacher, then distilling it into a cheaper bi-encoder student served online with offline-cached pin embeddings and realtime-cached query embeddings. They also show that VLM-generated captions and user-action features (board titles, high-engagement queries) improve relevance labels, and that relevance-tuned models yield reusable semantic embeddings.

takeaways.what_they_do: Train a large LLM teacher on a small human-labeled set, use it to label ~100x more sampled production data, then train a smaller student model on those soft labels and serve only the student.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we label using the teacher and we scale it up pretty much 100x
takeaways.numbers: ~100x data scaling; 8B model gave 12% over multilingual BERT and 20% over in-house embedding baseline

takeaways.what_they_do: Precompute expensive embeddings offline and only re-infer when inputs meaningfully change; cache realtime query embeddings since queries repeat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we get around an 85% cash hit rate
takeaways.numbers: ~85% cache hit rate on query embeddings

takeaways.technique: Enrich content with synthetic + behavioral annotations
takeaways.what_they_do: Augment raw text with VLM-generated captions and user-action signals (board titles, queries that drove engagement) as extra content annotations; ablation shows each addition helps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these two user action based features um serves as additional annotation for the content
takeaways.numbers: Sequential feature additions each improved relevance in ablation

takeaways.technique: Match model size to task, escalate only when needed
takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmarked multiple open-source LLMs and picked the one giving best performance for the task rather than defaulting to largest.

takeaways.technique: Small human-labeled gold set to anchor model choice
takeaways.what_they_do: Trained the teacher on a small set of human-annotator labels from specific segments, then measured gains against that anchored benchmark.
takeaways.evidence_quote: trained on a small set of human label data that we get from human annotators

takeaways.what_they_do: Relevance-tuned model embeddings are reused as general-purpose semantic representations for pins, queries, and boards across multiple surfaces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the pin embedding and the query embedding uh are basically free representations
